points.description: States one valid advantage of the observer over a filter, with correct reasoning. Acceptable: it uses the known input u and plant model so it predicts rather than differentiates, tracking velocity without the lag/smoothing trade-off of a low-pass filter; OR it estimates a state that is not measured, not merely a smoothed differentiated signal; OR quantisation enters through a bounded, filtered path rather than being divided by T. A bare assertion such as 'it is better/more accurate' with no reason does not earn the mark.

levels.says: Names a valid advantage (e.g. uses the model/input) but gives no reasoning or a muddled reason.

points.description: States one circumstance where the filter is safer, specifically invoking model error or parameter uncertainty. Acceptable: model-free so unaffected by wrong A, B or actuator gain (observer is biased by model error); plant parameters drift (temperature, load, wear) or strong nonlinearity away from linearisation point, making the observer's prediction misleading; a poorly identified model can make the observer diverge/be hard to diagnose. A circumstance not about model error/uncertainty (e.g. 'simpler to implement', 'cheaper') does not earn the mark.

levels.says: Says the filter is safer because it is simpler or does not need a model, but does not link this to model error, parameter uncertainty or drift.

rubric.notes: Full marks need one valid observer advantage with a reason and one filter-favouring circumstance tied to model error or parameter uncertainty. Half marks are for a correct but unreasoned or unspecific statement. Generic claims (simpler, cheaper) with no link to the model earn nothing on P2.
